en-US.title: Tend: Pixel Tomato Timer
en-US.shortDescription: A pixel tomato clock for deep work: one question, focus, then leave a note.
en-US.fullDescription:
One question. Go deeper.

Tend is a pixel tomato clock for thoughtful work: reading a paper, writing a chapter, working through a proof. Begin with one question, focus for a while, and leave a few words for your future self.

A LITTLE PIXEL ROOM
Big pixel digits, a ring of blocks that empties as the minutes pass, and a tomato that ripens from green to red while you stay with it. Quiet view hides everything else.

PICK ONE QUESTION
Choose one small question or task and, if you like, a stopping point. Keep a single intended result for the week in your notebook.

FIND YOUR RHYTHM
15/3, 25/5 or 50/10 minutes of focus and rest, or your own durations. Pause, continue or finish early. A longer break follows four full intervals.

PARK A THOUGHT
A new idea, a worry, another tab to open: write it down without leaving your question, and review it later.

LEAVE A THREAD
When a session ends, note what you learned, where you are stuck and the next small action. Every field is optional. Export the week's notes as Markdown, or keep a full backup that also opens in Tend on the web and on iPhone.

KNOWS WHEN TIME IS UP
Optional reminders reach you when the phone is locked, with a soft 8-bit chime when Tend is open. Reminders never show your notes.

ROOTED IN SOURCES
Short, linked notes on Deep Work, Slow Productivity, the Pomodoro Technique, if–then planning and research on breaks. Tend says which parts are its own adaptations; no interval is presented as best for everyone.

YOURS, ON YOUR DEVICE
Works offline. No account, no ads, no analytics, no AI service. Your notebook stays on your device until you export it.

Tend is an independent app by Houfu Chen, not affiliated with the authors it cites. Timer minutes record elapsed time, not attention or research quality.

contactEmail: (the developer email you register in Play Console)

appContent.appAccess: All functionality is available without special access (no account or login).
appContent.contentRating: IARC questionnaire: utility/productivity app, no violence, no user-to-user communication, no sharing of location, no purchases. Expected: Everyone / PEGI 3.
appContent.targetAudience: 13 and over (choosing under-13 brings in the Families policy; Tend is not designed for children).
appContent.dataSafety: No data collected, no data shared. The notebook is stored only on the device; exports go wherever the person sends them through Android's share sheet. Android Auto Backup may copy app data to the person's own Google account backup; that is not collection by the developer.
appContent.exactAlarms: Tend uses USE_EXACT_ALARM because its core function is a timer: the end-of-session reminder must ring at the deadline. If Play Console asks, declare 'Timer' as the core functionality.

reviewNotes:
No account, login, server or sample data is needed; everything works offline.

1. On Focus, tap Start focusing. A short sheet asks for one question; type anything and tap Start focusing.
2. On Android 13 and later, the first start asks for notification permission (used only for the end-of-session reminder while the app is in the background).
3. Pause / Continue keeps elapsed time. After a second or more, Finish early & reflect opens the reflection sheet: add optional notes and choose Save & finish, Save & start break, or Don't save this session (press twice).
4. Notebook shows saved sessions and parked thoughts; Export this week shares Markdown through the share sheet.
5. Settings: custom durations, chime, keep the screen awake, session reminders, backup export and restore.
6. Sources: attribution and links for the cited books and papers (paraphrased; no book text is reproduced). The tomato button at the top shows short source-linked reminders.
